Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 4.pdf ---
Minutia Deviation Tool (MDT)
So the deal is, we're working with the Defense Biometrics and Forensics folks and NIJ on
this broader contactless fingerprint research effort, and right now nobody has a good way
to actually compare two fingerprint captures side by side and see how much the minutiae
points drift between them. Like, you take a contact scan and a contactless scan of the
same finger, and you want to know objectively how far off the matching ridge features are
from one another — there's just no tool for that today. Researchers are basically eyeballing
it or doing something manual and clunky.
What I'm picturing is a pretty focused little desktop utility, nothing fancy, that lets a
researcher open up a pair of fingerprint files, see the image with all the minutiae points
overlaid on it, and then click on a point on one print and the matching point on the other
print, and the tool just calculates the spatial deviation between them and shows it right
there. They should be able to click into an individual minutia and see its details too — x, y
position, angle, classification, whatever annotations are attached to it.
It'd be nice if on top of that they could filter through the deviations somehow, like mark
pairs as they go, keep a running list during the session, and maybe filter the display based
on some deviation threshold they type in. And being able to export just the minutiae that
pass that filter into a new file would be great too — but honestly that filtering piece is more
of a nice-to-have, if it doesn't make it into the first version that's fine, it's not the core ask.
The core ask really is just the open-compare-calculate flow. Whatever they do during a
session, they need to be able to save it — both as a kind of session file they can reopen
later and pick up where they left off, and as a simple log file, something like a table they
could open in Excel, listing the pairs and the deviations calculated. Everything stays local,
opened and saved from the user's own machine — there's no need for this to talk to any
network or server, that's explicitly not something we want, keep it offline.
Who's going to use this is basically biometrics researchers — academia, government labs,
industry partners — people who already know what they're doing with fingerprint data, so
we don't need to dumb down the interface or build training wheels into it. This isn't a
public-facing product, it's a research instrument that we'll hand out to people who already
understand minutiae and EBTS-type files. Because of that, things like user accounts,
per-user permissions, fancy security layers — none of that matters here, skip it.
One more thing worth flagging: this is very much a prototype/beta-stage tool, not
something we're polishing for general release. It just needs to be stable enough that a
knowledgeable researcher can rely on it without us providing ongoing support afterwards
— once it's out the door, it's pretty much on its own. So let's not over-engineer it, just get
the comparison and measurement piece rock solid first.

Sistema: Minutia Deviation Tool (MDT)

Resumo executivo: The Minutia Deviation Tool (MDT) is an offline desktop research utility for objectively comparing minutiae from two fingerprint captures of the same finger, particularly contact and contactless captures. It enables biometrics researchers to inspect fingerprint images and minutiae, manually pair corresponding points, calculate spatial deviations, preserve comparison sessions, and export tabular measurement logs, replacing visual estimation and cumbersome manual processes.

Escopo: The MDT enables qualified biometrics researchers to compare two local fingerprint captures and measure the spatial deviation between corresponding minutiae.
  Em escopo: Loading two fingerprint files from local storage
  Em escopo: Side-by-side fingerprint image visualization
  Em escopo: Minutiae overlay on each fingerprint image
  Em escopo: Inspection of minutia coordinates, angle, classification, and annotations
  Em escopo: Manual pairing of corresponding minutiae
  Em escopo: Spatial deviation calculation and display
  Em escopo: Local saving and reopening of comparison sessions
  Em escopo: Export of an Excel-compatible tabular deviation log
  Em escopo: Optional marking, filtering, and filtered-minutiae export capabilities
  Fora de escopo: User accounts and authentication — explicitly unnecessary for the research utility
  Fora de escopo: Per-user permissions and role-based access control — explicitly excluded
  Fora de escopo: Network, cloud, or server communication — all processing and storage must remain local
  Fora de escopo: Automatic fingerprint matching — the scenario requires researchers to select corresponding minutiae manually
  Fora de escopo: Public-facing operation and beginner training workflows — users are expected to possess fingerprint-domain expertise
  Fora de escopo: Production-grade product support and continuous managed operation — the tool is a prototype/beta research instrument
  Premissa: PA-01: Researchers using the MDT understand fingerprint minutiae and EBTS-type fingerprint files.
  Premissa: PA-02: Each comparison uses two captures of the same finger.
  Premissa: PA-03: [INFERRED] Input files provide or reference both the fingerprint image and associated minutiae records.
  Premissa: PA-04: [INFERRED] Input coordinates are already expressed in a comparable coordinate system or include sufficient metadata for conversion.
  Premissa: PA-05: [TBD] The exact supported EBTS-type file formats and versions will be defined before implementation.
  Restrição: REST-01 (Architectural): The MDT must operate entirely offline without requiring a network or server.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Data location): All input, session, log, and exported files must be read from or written to user-selected local storage.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Platform): The solution must be delivered as a desktop utility.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Product maturity): The solution is a prototype/beta research instrument rather than a general-release product.
  Restrição: REST-05 (Scope): The first release must prioritize the open-compare-calculate workflow over optional filtering capabilities.
  Restrição: REST-06 (Access control): The solution must not require user accounts or per-user permissions.
  Restrição: REST-07 (Support): The delivered tool must be usable by qualified researchers without ongoing operational support.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Biometrics researcher (Usuário primário): Load fingerprint captures, inspect minutiae, pair corresponding points, measure deviations, preserve sessions, and export research results.
  STK-02 - Defense Biometrics and Forensics research stakeholders (Stakeholder externo): Obtain a reliable research instrument that supports objective analysis of contact and contactless fingerprint captures.
  STK-03 - National Institute of Justice (NIJ) (Stakeholder externo): Support the broader contactless fingerprint research effort with reproducible minutia-deviation measurements.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Comparison capture set: A comparison session concerns exactly two fingerprint captures of the same finger.
  RN-002 - Corresponding minutia pair: A valid comparison pair consists of one minutia from each fingerprint capture, selected as corresponding by the researcher.
  RN-003 - Spatial deviation calculation: [INFERRED] Spatial deviation is the Euclidean distance between the comparable x and y coordinates of the two minutiae in a valid pair.
  RN-004 - Minutia descriptive data: Available minutia information includes x position, y position, angle, classification, and attached annotations.
  RN-005 - Session continuity: A saved session preserves the researcher's comparison progress so work can resume later.
  RN-006 - Local data handling: Fingerprint data, comparison results, session data, and exported data remain on the researcher's local machine.
  RN-007 - Deviation threshold: [INFERRED] A minutia pair passes a deviation threshold when its calculated deviation is less than or equal to the researcher-entered threshold.
  RN-008 - Deviation log content: A comparison log lists the recorded minutia pairs and their calculated spatial deviations in tabular form.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Load comparison files: The system must load exactly two user-selected fingerprint files into a comparison session. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Display fingerprint images: The system must display the two loaded fingerprint images side by side. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Overlay minutiae: The system must overlay each fingerprint's available minutiae points on its displayed image. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Show minutia details: The system must display the available details of a researcher-selected minutia. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Register corresponding pair: The system must register one selected minutia from each fingerprint as a corresponding pair. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Calculate spatial deviation: The system must calculate the spatial deviation for each registered corresponding minutia pair. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Display spatial deviation: The system must display the calculated spatial deviation for the currently registered pair. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Mark a minutia pair: The system must allow the researcher to assign or remove a reviewed mark on a recorded minutia pair. [Could have]
  RF-009 - Maintain pair list: The system must maintain a visible session list of recorded minutia pairs and calculated deviations. [Could have]
  RF-010 - Filter by deviation threshold: The system must filter recorded minutia pairs using a researcher-entered deviation threshold. [Could have]
  RF-011 - Export filtered minutiae: The system must export the minutiae belonging to pairs that pass the active deviation filter into a new local file. [Could have]
  RF-012 - Save comparison session: The system must persist the current comparison session to a user-selected local session file. [Must have]
  RF-013 - Reopen comparison session: The system must restore a previously saved comparison session from a user-selected local session file. [Must have]
  RF-014 - Export deviation log: The system must export the recorded minutia pairs and calculated deviations to an Excel-compatible local tabular file. [Must have]
  RF-015 - Reject invalid input files: The system must reject an unreadable or unsupported fingerprint file with an explanatory error message. [Should have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Functional Suitability) - The system must calculate spatial deviations with an absolute error no greater than [TBD] 0.01 coordinate units against reference calculations. | Métrica: [TBD] At least 100 reference pairs tested with maximum absolute error of 0.01 coordinate units.
  RNF-002 (Performance Efficiency) - The system must load and display a pair of supported fingerprint files within [TBD] 3 seconds at the 95th percentile. | Métrica: [TBD] Maximum 3 seconds at the 95th percentile for files containing up to 500 minutiae each.
  RNF-003 (Performance Efficiency) - The system must calculate and display a selected pair's deviation within [TBD] 100 milliseconds at the 95th percentile. | Métrica: [TBD] Maximum 100 milliseconds at the 95th percentile across 1,000 calculations.
  RNF-004 (Reliability) - The system must complete [TBD] 100 consecutive open-compare-calculate-save workflows without an application crash. | Métrica: [TBD] Zero crashes during 100 consecutive core workflow executions.
  RNF-005 (Reliability) - The system must restore 100% of saved fingerprint references, recorded pairs, deviations, marks, and active filter values from a valid session file. | Métrica: 100% field equality across at least [TBD] 50 save-and-reopen test sessions.
  RNF-006 (Security) - The system must perform its workflows with zero outbound or inbound network connections. | Métrica: Zero network connection attempts during all functional and endurance test executions.
  RNF-007 (Interaction Capability) - The system must allow a qualified biometrics researcher to complete the open-compare-calculate workflow within [TBD] 2 minutes without external assistance. | Métrica: [TBD] At least 90% of five qualified researchers complete the workflow within 2 minutes.
  RNF-008 (Flexibility) - The system must install and launch on the [TBD] target desktop operating system without installing or configuring server components. | Métrica: 100% successful installation and launch across [TBD] five clean target desktop environments.

Histórias de usuário:
  HU-001 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero load two fingerprint files into one comparison session, para compare captures of the same finger
  HU-002 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero view both fingerprint images side by side, para visually relate corresponding ridge features
  HU-003 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero see minutiae overlaid on each fingerprint, para identify points available for comparison
  HU-004 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero inspect the details of an individual minutia, para understand its position and biometric attributes
  HU-005 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero pair corresponding minutiae from the two captures, para define which points must be measured against each other
  HU-006 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero calculate the spatial deviation of a minutia pair, para obtain an objective displacement measurement
  HU-007 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero see the calculated deviation immediately, para evaluate the selected pair during comparison
  HU-008 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero mark recorded pairs as reviewed, para track my progress through the comparison

  HU-011 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero export minutiae that pass the active filter, para reuse the selected subset in subsequent research
  HU-012 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero save my comparison session locally, para preserve my research progress

  HU-014 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero export an Excel-compatible deviation log, para analyze and report the measurements using tabular tools
  HU-015 - Como a biometrics researcher, quero receive a clear message when a fingerprint file cannot be loaded, para correct the input without corrupting the session

Casos de uso:
  UC-001 - Load fingerprint comparison | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher starts a new comparison.
    2. The system requests two local fingerprint files.
    3. The researcher selects the files.
    4. The system validates and loads both files.
    5. The system creates the comparison session.
  UC-002 - Inspect fingerprint minutiae | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The system displays the images with minutiae overlays.
    2. The researcher selects a minutia.
    3. The system highlights the selected point.
    4. The system displays its x position, y position, angle, classification, and annotations.
  UC-003 - Pair and measure minutiae | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher selects a minutia from the first fingerprint.
    2. The researcher selects the corresponding minutia from the second fingerprint.
    3. The system registers the corresponding pair.
    4. The system calculates the spatial deviation.
    5. The system displays and records the deviation.
  UC-004 - Manage recorded pairs | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher opens the session pair list.
    2. The system displays all recorded pairs and deviations.
    3. The researcher selects a pair.
    4. The researcher assigns or removes its reviewed mark.
    5. The system updates the pair list.
  UC-005 - Filter and export minutiae | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher enters a deviation threshold.
    2. The system validates the threshold.
    3. The system displays pairs whose deviations are less than or equal to the threshold.
    4. The researcher requests filtered-minutiae export.
    5. The system writes the qualifying minutiae to a local file.
  UC-006 - Save comparison session | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher requests session saving.
    2. The system requests a local destination.
    3. The researcher selects the destination.
    4. The system writes the complete session state.
    5. The system confirms successful saving.
  UC-007 - Reopen comparison session | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher requests to open a session.
    2. The system requests a local session file.
    3. The researcher selects the file.
    4. The system validates the session file.
    5. The system restores the fingerprint references, pairs, deviations, marks, and filter values.
  UC-008 - Export deviation log | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher requests log export.
    2. The system requests a local destination.
    3. The researcher selects the destination.
    4. The system writes one tabular record per minutia pair.
    5. The system confirms successful export.

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado two supported local fingerprint files containing image and minutia data, quando the researcher selects both files for a new comparison, então the system creates one session containing exactly two loaded fingerprint captures
  CA-002 - Dado two fingerprint files have been loaded, quando the comparison view opens, então the system displays both fingerprint images simultaneously in separate side-by-side panels
  CA-003 - Dado a loaded fingerprint contains minutia records, quando its image is displayed, então the system renders one visible overlay marker for every parsed minutia record
  CA-004 - Dado a minutia marker is visible, quando the researcher selects the marker, então the system displays its x position, y position, angle, classification, and each available annotation, marking absent fields as unavailable
  CA-005 - Dado one minutia is available on each displayed fingerprint, quando the researcher selects one point from each capture, então the system records exactly one pair containing the two selected minutia identifiers
  CA-006 - Dado a valid pair has coordinates (x1, y1) and (x2, y2), quando the pair is registered, então the system records a deviation equal to the square root of ((x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²), within [TBD] 0.01 coordinate units
  CA-007 - Dado a deviation has been calculated for the current pair, quando calculation completes, então the system displays the numeric deviation and its coordinate unit within [TBD] 100 milliseconds
  CA-008 - Dado a recorded pair is selected, quando the researcher toggles its reviewed mark, então the system changes the pair's reviewed status to the opposite Boolean value and displays the updated status
  CA-009 - Dado three pairs have been recorded, quando the researcher opens the pair list, então the system displays exactly three entries, each containing both minutia identifiers and its calculated deviation
  CA-010 - Dado recorded deviations are 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0 coordinate units, quando the researcher applies a threshold of 2.0, então the system displays exactly the pairs with deviations 1.0 and 2.0
  CA-011 - Dado two pairs pass the active deviation filter, quando the researcher exports filtered minutiae, então the system creates one local file containing only the minutiae belonging to those two qualifying pairs
  CA-012 - Dado an open session contains fingerprints, pairs, deviations, marks, and a filter value, quando the researcher saves the session to a writable local destination, então the system creates one session file containing 100% of the current comparison state and displays a success confirmation
  CA-013 - Dado a valid previously saved session file exists, quando the researcher opens the file, então the system restores 100% of its fingerprint references, pairs, deviations, marks, and filter values
  CA-014 - Dado a session contains five recorded pairs with calculated deviations, quando the researcher exports the deviation log, então the system creates a local CSV or [TBD] equivalent Excel-compatible file containing one header row and exactly five data rows
  CA-015 - Dado the researcher selects an unreadable or unsupported file, quando the system validates the file, então the system displays the message 'Fingerprint file could not be loaded: unsupported or unreadable format' and does not add the file to the session

Glossário:
  Minutia: A localized fingerprint ridge characteristic represented by coordinates and related attributes such as angle and classification.
  Minutiae: The plural form of minutia; the set of localized ridge characteristics associated with a fingerprint.
  Spatial deviation: The measured distance between the comparable positions of two corresponding minutiae.
  Corresponding pair: One minutia from each fingerprint capture identified by the researcher as representing the same ridge feature.
  Contact fingerprint capture: A fingerprint image acquired while the finger physically contacts the capture surface.
  Contactless fingerprint capture: A fingerprint image acquired without the finger physically contacting the capture device.
  EBTS-type file: A fingerprint-data file conforming to an Electronic Biometric Transmission Specification or related supported format; exact formats are [TBD].
  Comparison session: The locally maintained working state containing two fingerprint captures, recorded pairs, deviations, marks, and filter settings.
  Deviation threshold: A non-negative researcher-entered limit used to include pairs whose calculated deviation is less than or equal to that value.
  Deviation log: An Excel-compatible tabular file listing recorded minutia pairs and their calculated spatial deviations.

O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.

Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2 — Características do requisito individual
• Necessário: Existe uma necessidade real que o justifica. Sem o requisito, há uma lacuna de negócio.
• Não ambíguo: Tem uma única interpretação possível. Evitar: 'eficiente', 'fácil', 'rápido', 'amigável'.
• Verificável: Pode ser testado objetivamente com critério mensurável. 'Rápido' não é verificável; '< 2 s' é.
• Singular: Descreve uma única coisa. Nunca usar 'e' ou 'ou' para combinar dois comportamentos em um 
RF.
• Viável: Tecnicamente e financeiramente possível dentro das restrições do projeto.
• Rastreável: Tem origem (stakeholder ou RN) e destino (caso de teste) identificados.
• Completo: Contém todas as informações necessárias para implementação sem consultas adicionais.
• Consistente: Não conflita com nenhum outro requisito do documento.

Minutia Deviation Tool (MDT)
So the deal is, we're working with the Defense Biometrics and Forensics folks and NIJ on
this broader contactless fingerprint research effort, and right now nobody has a good way
to actually compare two fingerprint captures side by side and see how much the minutiae
points drift between them. Like, you take a contact scan and a contactless scan of the
same finger, and you want to know objectively how far off the matching ridge features are
from one another — there's just no tool for that today. Researchers are basically eyeballing
it or doing something manual and clunky.
What I'm picturing is a pretty focused little desktop utility, nothing fancy, that lets a
researcher open up a pair of fingerprint files, see the image with all the minutiae points
overlaid on it, and then click on a point on one print and the matching point on the other
print, and the tool just calculates the spatial deviation between them and shows it right
there. They should be able to click into an individual minutia and see its details too — x, y
position, angle, classification, whatever annotations are attached to it.
It'd be nice if on top of that they could filter through the deviations somehow, like mark
pairs as they go, keep a running list during the session, and maybe filter the display based
on some deviation threshold they type in. And being able to export just the minutiae that
pass that filter into a new file would be great too — but honestly that filtering piece is more
of a nice-to-have, if it doesn't make it into the first version that's fine, it's not the core ask.
The core ask really is just the open-compare-calculate flow. Whatever they do during a
session, they need to be able to save it — both as a kind of session file they can reopen
later and pick up where they left off, and as a simple log file, something like a table they
could open in Excel, listing the pairs and the deviations calculated. Everything stays local,
opened and saved from the user's own machine — there's no need for this to talk to any
network or server, that's explicitly not something we want, keep it offline.
Who's going to use this is basically biometrics researchers — academia, government labs,
industry partners — people who already know what they're doing with fingerprint data, so
we don't need to dumb down the interface or build training wheels into it. This isn't a
public-facing product, it's a research instrument that we'll hand out to people who already
understand minutiae and EBTS-type files. Because of that, things like user accounts,
per-user permissions, fancy security layers — none of that matters here, skip it.
One more thing worth flagging: this is very much a prototype/beta-stage tool, not
something we're polishing for general release. It just needs to be stable enough that a
knowledgeable researcher can rely on it without us providing ongoing support afterwards
— once it's out the door, it's pretty much on its own. So let's not over-engineer it, just get
the comparison and measurement piece rock solid first.

Condições prévias para a criatividade
A criatividade surge não por ordem, mas por acaso. É mais provável que a criatividade 
ocorra quando todas as quatro condições prévias a seguir forem atendidas [KrSc2017]:
▪ Chance – e, portanto, tempo – para que uma ideia surja
▪ Conhecimento do assunto, o que aumenta as chances de uma ideia que faça a

▪ Motivação, pois o nosso cérebro só pode ser criativo se houver um benefício direto

3.2.1 Brainstorming (L3)
O brainstorming foi desenvolvido nas décadas de 1940 e 1950 por Alex F. Osborn 
[Osbo1979]. Como a maioria das técnicas de criatividade, o ponto crucial do brainstorming é 
a separação entre a descoberta de ideias e a análise de ideias. É realizado em grupos de 
cerca de 5 a 10 pessoas e dura cerca de 20 minutos. Um moderador garante a condução 
ordenada do brainstorming e a documentação das ideias.
Muitas variantes diferentes evoluíram ao longo do tempo, por exemplo, paradoxo do 
brainstorming, método 6-3-5, brainwriting.
3.2.2 Técnicas de analogia (L2)
As técnicas de analogia (p. ex., a bissociação [Koes1964]) são técnicas que ajudam a ter 
ideias para tópicos críticos e complexos. Eles usam analogias para apoiar o pensamento e 
gerar ideias. Seu sucesso ou fracasso é influenciado principalmente pela qualidade da 
analogia. A relevância de sistemas semelhantes é discutida em 2.4.
3.2.3 Prototipagem (L3)
Prototipagem é um termo abrangente e refere-se à criação de vários tipos de amostras ou 
modelos iniciais construídos para obter experiências ao vivo com um conceito ou processo.
Para a elicitação de requisitos, o termo protótipo intencionalmente não se refere apenas à 
implementação de protótipos em software. Em vez disso, também se refere a tudo que 
possa representar os requisitos de um sistema a ser desenvolvido (p. ex., esboço da 
interface do usuário, maquete física, vídeo). O objetivo da prototipagem na elicitação de 
requisitos é a simulação do novo sistema e a exploração dos requisitos por meio da 
estimulação de concordância e objeção ou esclarecimento e alteração.

O valor de um requisito é igual ao seu benefício menos o custo para elicitar, documentar,

Princípio 2 - Stakeholders: ER é a satisfação dos desejos e 
necessidades dos stakeholders
Como a ER trata de compreender os desejos e necessidades dos stakeholders, lidar 
devidamente com eles é uma tarefa essencial da ER. Cada stakeholder tem um papel no 
contexto do sistema a ser construído, por exemplo, usuário, cliente, operador ou regulador.
Um stakeholder também pode ter mais de um papel simultaneamente. Para papéis de 
stakeholders com muitos indivíduos ou quando estes são desconhecidos, a descrição 
fictícia conhecida como personas pode ser definida como substituta. Não é suficiente 
considerar apenas os requisitos dos usuários finais ou clientes. Fazer isso significaria que 
poderíamos negligenciar requisitos críticos de outros stakeholders. Os usuários que 
proveem feedback sobre o uso do sistema também são considerados stakeholders.
Os stakeholders podem ter necessidades e pontos de vista diferentes, o que resulta em 
requisitos conflitantes. É uma tarefa da ER identificar e resolver tais conflitos.
Envolver as pessoas certas nos papéis relevantes de stakeholder é crucial para o sucesso da 
ER. As práticas para identificar, priorizar e trabalhar com stakeholders são descritas em 4.

1.3 Princípios Fundamentais de Qualidade de Requisitos
Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2 — Características do requisito individual
• Necessário: Existe uma necessidade real que o justifica. Sem o requisito, há uma lacuna de negócio.
• Não ambíguo: Tem uma única interpretação possível. Evitar: 'eficiente', 'fácil', 'rápido', 'amigável'.
• Verificável: Pode ser testado objetivamente com critério mensurável. 'Rápido' não é verificável; '< 2 s' é.
• Singular: Descreve uma única coisa. Nunca usar 'e' ou 'ou' para combinar dois comportamentos em um 
RF.
• Viável: Tecnicamente e financeiramente possível dentro das restrições do projeto.
• Rastreável: Tem origem (stakeholder ou RN) e destino (caso de teste) identificados.
• Completo: Contém todas as informações necessárias para implementação sem consultas adicionais.
• Consistente: Não conflita com nenhum outro requisito do documento.
• Priorizado: Tem um nível de prioridade definido (MoSCoW: Must/Should/Could/Won't).PARTE 2 — Padrões de Escrita por Artefato

1.2 Fatores relevantes para a abordagem de elicitação de 
planejamento e resolução de conflitos (L2)
A literatura sobre estimativa de software [McCo2006] e os resultados da prática industrial 
colocam muita responsabilidade na disciplina de Engenharia de Requisitos para atingir os 
objetivos gerais de desenvolvimento. Do ponto de vista da Engenharia de Requisitos, uma 
parte significativa dessa responsabilidade deve ser atribuída à elicitação de requisitos e à 
resolução de conflitos.
Ambos exigem uma abordagem de planejamento específica devido aos seguintes desafios:
▪ A elicitação de requisitos não pode ser planejada apenas com base no tamanho 
esperado do resultado, pois nenhuma expectativa realista está disponível no início da 
elicitação.
▪ Os conflitos de requisitos não podem ser planejados ou previstos. O Engenheiro de

GABARITO — Project Scenario 4: MDT (Minutia Deviation Tool)
Use: "ground_truth" field for RAGAS (context_precision / context_recall).
Each line is an atomic, checkable claim against the scenario text and the
knowledge base — not a full SRS, just the set of facts a well-grounded SRS
for this scenario should be able to cover.

- The tool lets a researcher open a pair of fingerprint files and view their minutiae points overlaid on the image.
- Clicking a point on one print and the matching point on the other calculates and displays the spatial deviation between them.
- Clicking an individual minutia shows its details: x/y position, angle, classification, and any annotations.
- Marking/filtering deviation pairs and exporting the filtered minutiae is a nice-to-have, not required for the first version.
- The core required flow is: open files, compare corresponding points, calculate deviation.
- A session can be saved as a session file that can be reopened later.
- A session can also be saved as a simple log file (table format, e.g. openable in Excel) listing the pairs and calculated deviations.
- The tool must work entirely offline and locally; it must not require any network or server communication.
- The intended users are biometrics researchers in academia, government labs, and industry, already familiar with minutiae and EBTS-type files.
- The interface does not need to be simplified for non-expert users.
- User accounts, per-user permissions, and security layers are explicitly out of scope.
- This is a prototype/beta-stage tool, not intended for general release or for ongoing developer support after delivery.

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: At least one minutia pair has been recorded.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The pair list reflects the current recorded pairs, deviations, and review marks.
fluxo_principal: 1. The researcher opens the session pair list.
2. The system displays all recorded pairs and deviations.
3. The researcher selects a pair.
4. The researcher assigns or removes its reviewed mark.
5. The system updates the pair list.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. The researcher makes no marking change → the system preserves the current mark.
fluxos_excecao: 1a. No pairs are recorded → the system displays an empty list.

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The session contains at least one pair with a calculated deviation.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: Pairs satisfying the threshold are displayed and may be exported to a local file.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No export file is created and existing session data remains unchanged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The researcher enters a deviation threshold.
2. The system validates the threshold.
3. The system displays pairs whose deviations are less than or equal to the threshold.
4. The researcher requests filtered-minutiae export.
5. The system writes the qualifying minutiae to a local file.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. No pair passes the threshold → the system displays an empty filtered result.
fluxos_excecao: 2a. The threshold is not a non-negative number → the system rejects it and preserves the previous filter (ref. RN-007, RF-010).
5a. The destination cannot be written → the system reports the failure and creates no partial export file.

casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The current comparison state is stored in the selected local session file.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The current session remains open and no incomplete session file is retained.
fluxo_principal: 1. The researcher requests session saving.
2. The system requests a local destination.
3. The researcher selects the destination.
4. The system writes the complete session state.
5. The system confirms successful saving.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The researcher cancels destination selection → the system returns to the open session without saving.
fluxos_excecao: 4a. The destination is not writable → the system reports the error and preserves the in-memory session (ref. RN-005, RF-012).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A valid MDT session file exists on local storage.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The saved comparison state is restored.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The current application state remains unchanged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The researcher requests to open a session.
2. The system requests a local session file.
3. The researcher selects the file.
4. The system validates the session file.
5. The system restores the fingerprint references, pairs, deviations, marks, and filter values.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The researcher cancels selection → the system retains the current state.
fluxos_excecao: 4a. The session file is invalid or corrupted → the system reports the error and does not partially restore it (ref. RN-005, RF-013).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The session contains at least one recorded minutia pair with a calculated deviation.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: An Excel-compatible tabular log is written to the selected local destination.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No incomplete log file is retained.
fluxo_principal: 1. The researcher requests log export.
2. The system requests a local destination.
3. The researcher selects the destination.
4. The system writes one tabular record per minutia pair.
5. The system confirms successful export.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The researcher cancels selection → the system returns to the session without exporting.
fluxos_excecao: 4a. The destination cannot be written → the system reports the error and creates no partial log (ref. RN-008, RF-014).

premissas: PA-01: Users already have prior familiarity with minutiae and EBTS-format files.
PA-02: [INFERRED] The tool runs as a local desktop utility, with no need for server installation.
restricoes: REST-01 (Scope): It is a prototype/beta-stage tool, not intended for general release nor for ongoing developer support after delivery.

stakeholders.descricao: Biometrics researcher (academia, government labs, industry) — the sole user type, already familiar with minutiae and EBTS files; the interface does not need to be simplified for them.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The pair marking/filtering-by-deviation-threshold and filtered export feature is optional (nice-to-have) — only the open-compare-calculate flow is required for the first version.
The tool must operate entirely offline and locally — network or server communication is not permitted.
The interface does not need to be simplified for non-expert users — the target audience already understands minutiae and EBTS files.
User accounts, per-user permissions, and security layers are explicitly out of scope.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must allow the researcher to open a pair of fingerprint files.
The system must display each fingerprint image with its minutiae points overlaid.
The system must allow the researcher to click a point on one print and the corresponding point on the other print.
The system must calculate and display the spatial deviation between two selected corresponding minutiae points.
The system must allow the researcher to click an individual minutia and view its details (x/y position, angle, classification, annotations).
The system must allow the researcher to save the current session as a session file that can be reopened later.
The system must allow the researcher to save the session as a table-format log file (e.g., openable in Excel), listing the compared pairs and calculated deviations.
The system must allow the researcher to mark/filter deviation pairs by a threshold entered during the session — optional, nice-to-have (see RN-001).
The system must allow the researcher to export, to a new file, only the minutiae that pass the threshold filter — optional, nice-to-have (see RN-001).

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must operate entirely offline and locally, without requiring any network or server communication.
requisitos_nao_funcionais.metrica_aceitacao: All core functions (open, compare, save) work with the network disconnected

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The tool, even at prototype/beta stage, must be stable enough for an experienced researcher to rely on it without ongoing developer support after delivery.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a biometrics researcher, I want to open a pair of fingerprint files, so that I can compare their minutiae.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to see minutiae points overlaid on the images, so that I can visually identify corresponding points.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to click matching points on both prints and see the calculated spatial deviation, so that I can objectively measure how much the minutiae drifted between captures.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to click an individual minutia and see its details, so that I can inspect it closely.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to save my session and reopen it later, so that I can continue my work without losing progress.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to export a log with the compared pairs and deviations, so that I can analyze the results in a spreadsheet.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Compare fingerprint pair — the researcher opens two files, views the overlaid minutiae, selects corresponding points, and the system calculates and displays the deviation.
Save and resume session — the researcher saves the current session to a file and reopens it later to continue the work.
Export comparison log — the researcher exports a table-format log with all compared pairs and their deviations.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given two fingerprint files open with minutiae overlaid, when the researcher clicks a point on each print, then the system calculates and displays the spatial deviation between them.
Given a selected minutia point, when the researcher clicks it, then the system displays its x/y position, angle, classification, and any annotations.
Given an active session, when the researcher saves it as a session file, then the session can later be reopened with all prior comparisons intact.
Given a completed session, when the researcher exports the log, then the file lists all compared pairs and their calculated deviations in a table format openable in a spreadsheet.
Given the tool is running with no network connection, when the researcher performs any core operation (open, compare, save), then the tool functions normally without requiring network access.
